chapter: Benny Meroff and Chicago's jazz scene
title: Meroff's road show: personnel, Corn Palace, trunks and twelve outfits
summary: The touring band has Red Pepper and Mousey Powell, plays comedy and opera bits, and carries its own stage, instrument trunks and twelve outfits per man.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: ---so we could all have fun with the girls, you know and so on. But, that was a very good band; we had Red Pepper, who is a great trumpet player; and we had a little trombone player, who played - Mouse Powell---
Mousey Powell---

Mousey Powell and his "Neon" trombone and, of course, we went right on doing the show---Meroff carried his own stage -- we set up a whole stage whenever we went - it was all done by train. And, if we played in the ballroom a big stage was set up. And, I think, there's a picture you have of me in front of the Corn Palace---
Yes, in Mitchell, South Dakota.
I didn't count the number of men but we had a pretty good size band---
About twenty (20) people, I guess---
Yeah---
18 or something.
But, we still had to do our same old
things, you know -- we had to do little dancing and even sang from Rigolelto.
Operatic---

Operatic - in comedy and all these things. And, we did that but now we're getting down -- we had gone through Columbus, Ohio, and Cleveland and all those places and, I must say, that that was an outstanding band. You know, it was just--- it was a show like you can't believe.
You couldn't compare that band with Steinberg or the Chub Steinberg or---Seattle Harmony Band---
Oh - no---
It was a totally different bag - wasn't it---
Yeah - a different bag but not only that but sensational musicians - the top musicians in the field at that time---
Right.

And, I remember, we all-- this is interesting because it was interesting to me even then, he had trunks made -- and all our instruments fit right in little grooves in shelves in these great big steamer trunks---
To go on the train---

To go on the trains; he even had the great big wooden one made for the string bass and the tuba and all that stuff -- of course, that all went on the train and, uh, and the -- oh, the costumes - yeah - we wore
what you call Eaton jackets --
Oh, yes.
And--- with tuxedo pants and a stiff shirt with a black artist kind of a tie and he had--- we had twelve outfits - each guy---
Twelve?

Twelve different outfits and he'd say - all right, next show we use--- you wear the white Eaton$- and maybe the next day, we'd wear the blue Eaton$-- and maybe in the middle of the show, where there was a break, we'd change from the whites to the black ones --
My God---
